messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV_CACHE_EVICTION_RATE_HIGH fired in prod (us-west-2). Pager routed to @oncall. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/8921

maria: got the page, I'm on it. checking dashboard now — can someone grab QPS for the generation path?

jon: looking — generation QPS steady at ~450 rps, but kv_cache hit_rate dropped from 98% -> 61% around 12:04 UTC. eviction_rate spiked to ~240/s. p95 token latency up from 80ms -> 290ms.

ashley: any deployments/infra changes in the last 30m?

maria: nothing in prod deploy logs. I see a config push to cache TTL in staging earlier but not prod.

kevin: adding the runbook snippet: if eviction_rate > 200/s and hit_rate < 75% -> check memory pressure on gpu-hosts and cache node OOMs, and consider increasing cache capacity or short-term TTL bump.

jon: cpu/mem on cache nodes show increased memory eviction: host cache-02 shows kernel OOM kills for user process (see logs). Possibly a memory leak in the LRU worker thread.

maria: ok. plan: 1) mute noisy eviction alert for 15m to reduce paging while we triage 2) spin up 2 temporary cache replicas in us-west-2 and attach 10GB extra cache each 3) enable synchronous fallback to persistent store for heavy keys to reduce pressure. Who can create the replicas?

ashley: I can create replicas, starting now. will update when healthy.

kevin: I'll open a quick alert refinement PR. Current alert expression is too broad. Proposed change in PromQL:

```
# current noisy rule (matches many short spikes)
kv_cache_eviction_rate_total{env="prod"} > 100

# proposed: sustained high eviction over 2m and low hit rate
sum(rate(kv_cache_eviction_rate_total{env="prod"}[2m])) by (cluster) > 150
and
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate{env="prod"}[5m]) < 0.80
```

kevin: this will reduce noise and only fire when evictions are sustained AND hit rate is degraded. I'll put the PR up and link it here.

jon: Ashley's replicas are reporting healthy in ~20s. Handoff to warm them with top prefixes. Running cache-warm job for the top-200 keys by QPS.

maria: starting fallback to persistent store for keys with >5 misses/sec to throttle cache-thrashing. This will add ~30ms extra to those requests but should stabilize latency.

incident-bot: :information_source: Mute applied to alert KV_CACHE_EVICTION_RATE_HIGH by kevin for 15m (reason: active mitigation)

eva: FYI customer_123 (large embeddings index) saw timeouts, traced to retry storms while cache warmed. We notified their solutions contact at 12:15 UTC and opened support case #SUP-881.

maria: quick impact summary for handoff: customers: intermittent 5-10% of generation requests for some customers experienced 2-4s additional latency, a handful of timeouts (~40 errors over 30m). Root cause: sudden cache eviction spree (likely process-level memory leak) -> hit rate collapse -> backend load amplification.

sre-rotation: taking over the incident at 12:30 UTC. High-level: replicas up, fallback enabled, cache-warm job running. Current metrics: hit_rate recovering to ~85%, eviction_rate down to ~60/s, p95 latency still ~180ms.

kevin: created alert refinement PR: https://git.redwood.example/infra/alerts/pulls/422 — reviewers: @maria @jon. Also added a new dashboard panel suggestion: KV Cache Overview with panels: hit_rate (5m), eviction_rate (1m), mem_pressure, top-evicted-keys.

jon: new dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv-cache/kv-cache-overview?orgId=1 — I've added an annotation at 12:04 for the spike.

ashley: logs show the LRU worker process on cache-02 restarted by k8s at 12:07 due to OOM. Opening an infra issue to track potential memory leak: https://issues.redwood.example/INFRA-719

maria: follow-ups before this is closed: 1) refine alert rule (kevin) 2) add eviction_count alert (sustained + correlate with hit_rate) (jon) 3) postmortem + timeline (maria) 4) runbook update: add cache replica spin-up steps and fallback enabling command (ashley) 5) prod patch for LRU worker memory leak investigation (infra)

eva: tagging customer impact in the postmortem template. Adding note to support case.

sre-rotation: I'll keep monitoring, will escalate to SEV2 if tail latency doesn't drop below 120ms within next 30m. For handoff notes to next oncall: replicas present, fallback rule in place (`cache.fallback=true`), PR for alert refinement in review, INFRA-719 open.

maria: thanks everyone. if latency trends down and eviction_rate stays low for 45m we'll close the thread and mark RCA start.

kevin: added an automated alert for cache-eviction-to-hitrate regression: fires when
```
(avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate{env="prod"}[10m]) - kv_cache_hit_rate{env="prod"}) > 0.15
```
This will catch sudden drops and can be used to trigger cache-warm rather than straight paging.

jon: note for post-incident tuning: adjust default TTL for large embedding keys to longer (from 5m -> 30m) to reduce churn, and consider per-key weight eviction adjustments.

maria: closing notes: incident downgraded, stabilization observed. We'll do the full write-up tomorrow. Great job on the fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
